editorial.marketOverview: The three-day Nasdaq/QQQ baseline remains bearish after Friday's severe semiconductor-led selling. Positive US futures indicate a possible oversold Monday rebound, but US cash markets have not confirmed it; Korean chip shares remain weak.
editorial.whatChanged: Reuters November 23 reported Brent $92.29 and WTI $83.26 per barrel, both modestly lower despite refinery and shipping attack headlines. These newer article-time oil indications differ from earlier WSJ reports and are not matched futures ticks. No new curated Open Watch event or material directional shift was verified.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Positive US futures versus weak Asian chip cash markets suggest tactical short covering rather than confirmed leadership repair. Oil weakness may relieve inflation pressure, but geopolitical supply risks persist. The previously indicated 29 bp Treasury spread is stale; matched yields, FedWatch, VXN/VIX and US breadth are not available.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23 may open with an oversold relief bounce, with flash PMIs potentially altering rate expectations. Tuesday November 24 tests QQQ/SOX/SMH breadth follow-through around consumer confidence and Dell earnings. Wednesday November 25 brings PCE, GDP, durable goods, claims and the Fed Beige Book, making rates-sensitive technology vulnerable to surprises. These are conditional scenarios, not realized returns.
editorial.bullCase: A durable rebound requires simultaneous US cash-session QQQ and SOX/SMH strength, improving breadth, declining VXN/VIX and stable or falling verified yields. Benign PMIs and PCE plus credible AI-hardware earnings guidance could extend the bounce.
editorial.bearCase: A failed futures-led gap-up, renewed semiconductor underperformance and weak breadth favor bearish continuation. Higher verified yields or hotter inflation would intensify valuation pressure; oil-supply disruptions could compound risk.
